findings.title: Inside India newsletter: India’s green push aims to boost energy security but exposes China dependency - CNBC
findings.reason: The article reports that India relies on China for nearly 80% of its battery-based energy storage solutions to support its renewable energy expansion, highlighting sustained demand and market dominance for China's new energy sector.

articles.title: Bank of Japan Hikes as Expected: What Comes After 1.0%?
articles.claim_summary: BOJ raised its policy rate to 1.0%, reflecting growing confidence in Japan's economic normalisation, with further gradual hikes likely.

findings.title: BOJ may be forced to hike rates rapidly if inflation accelerates, board member Masu says - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: BOJ board member Kazuyuki Masu stated that he is 'convinced the BOJ needs to raise its policy rate further' as underlying inflation nears the 2% target, warning that rates may need to rise rapidly if price pressures accelerate.

findings.title: Rising Japanese yields may keep more domestic money at home, Fitch says - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: The report notes that markets have priced in a near certainty that the Bank of Japan will raise its key rate to 1.25% at its upcoming meeting, and Fitch Ratings stated it expects policy rates to rise faster than consensus in 2026 and 2027.

articles.title: BOJ’s Hawkish Hold: Another 2026 Hike Is Still on the Table
articles.claim_summary: The Bank of Japan maintained its policy interest rate in a hawkish hold, projecting core inflation at or above 2% through its entire forecast horizon with upside price risks. Despite an apparent downgrade to near-term inflation caused by temporary government subsidies, the central bank's underlying policy outlook remains unchanged, keeping additional rate hikes through 2026 on the table.

findings.title: BOJ may be forced to hike rates rapidly if inflation accelerates, board member Masu says - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: BOJ board member Kazuyuki Masu stated that broadening price pressures have pushed underlying inflation 'very close' to its 2% target and affirmed that he is convinced the BOJ needs to raise its policy rate further, citing upside risks to inflation.

articles.title: Malaysia Sector Outlook: Construction - Year of Execution
articles.claim_summary: 2026 is the Malaysian construction sector's "Execution Year": record 2025 contract awards (RM202.5 billion) are expected to translate into peak earnings delivery for major contractors. Budget 2026 development expenditure eases to RM81 billion (from RM86 billion in 2025), but the 13th Malaysia Plan maintains a RM430 billion total allocation through 2030, sustaining infrastructure commitment. Data centres remain the key structural growth driver alongside transport, industrial parks and renewable energy projects; margin risks from steel/cement/labour inflation are seen as manageable given strong order books.

findings.title: Paragon Globe secures RM45 mil contract for Johor data centre development - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: Paragon Globe announced securing a RM45.16 million contract for earthworks and retaining walls for a data centre in Johor targeted for completion by late 2026, supporting the claim that data centres are driving sector order execution.

findings.title: RHB IB estimates federal govt’s 2027 budget allocation at RM437.8 bil - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: RHB IB notes federal development expenditure of RM81 billion and highlights that the national budget will focus on infrastructure development, corroborating the claim's figures and sustained infrastructure commitment.

articles.title: Top & Bottom Bond Funds 2Q26: Bond Markets Rebound, but Rate Risks Remain
articles.claim_summary: Bond funds staged a broad rebound in 2Q26 as pressures from an earlier energy shock subsided, though persistent interest rate risks make short-to-medium duration bonds and investment-grade credit the optimal allocation strategy.

findings.title: Weak Southeast Asia bond auctions offer buying chance, funds say - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: Desmond Fu of Western Asset Management explicitly confirms that they 'prefer short- to intermediate-maturity bonds' because longer-dated bonds remain vulnerable to global term-premium shocks and heavy issuance.

findings.title: Where investors are finding income outside traditional bonds as brutal drawdown drags on - CNBC
findings.reason: Financial advisors and strategists cited in the article confirm that bonds should remain part of diversified portfolios but advocate 'shifting allocation to lower-duration alternatives such as ultra-short bonds' due to inflation and rising interest rate risks.
